data.long_meaning: The name Rawley is derived from the Old English word 'Raedwald', which means 'ruler' and 'red'. This name was given to a king of East Anglia in the 6th century. In Christian tradition, Rawley symbolizes courage, determination, and strength in the face of adversity. The name Rawley carries the meaning “Ruler of the Red” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Rawley usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler of the red and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_english.name: Rawley
in_english.long_meaning: A name derived from the Old English words 'hraewel' (noble, powerful) and 'leah' (wood, clearing). It may also be derived from the Old English words 'raw' (red) and 'leah' (wood, clearing). Both derivations mean 'Red Clearing' or 'Noble Clearing'. However, the modern English name 'Rawley' is more likely derived from the first meaning.
